blocks.h2: What Does a Catch Basin Do?
blocks.body: A catch basin is a box in the ground with a grate on top. It collects rain from your yard, driveway or downspouts and sends it to a storm line. Its bottom sits below the outlet, so leaves and silt settle there. When the bottom fills, the outlet clogs and water stays on the surface.

img.alt: Diagram of a catch basin showing the inlet grate, water line, sediment settling in the sump and the outlet pipe carrying water away

blocks.h2: Catch Basin Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: How often should a catch basin be cleaned?
items.preview: At least once a year, after the leaves fall.
items.answer: At least once a year in late fall. Yards with big trees may need a spring cleaning too.

items.q: Can a clogged catch basin cause basement water?
items.answer: Yes. Water that pools near the house soaks into the soil and can find its way through older foundations or into your [sump pump](/geneva/sump-pumps) pit.

items.q: Is the catch basin in my yard mine to maintain?
items.preview: Usually, if it drains your property.
items.answer: Usually. If it's on your property and handles your yard or driveway, it's yours.

items.q: Can you replace a broken grate?
items.answer: Yes. We replace grates and repair cracked basin walls.

items.q: Can you add a catch basin where water pools?
items.preview: Yes, if there's somewhere to drain it.
items.answer: Yes, if there's a storm line or outlet to connect to. We'll look at the yard and tell you what's possible.

items.q: How much does catch basin repair cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on the work. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on whether it needs cleaning, a grate, wall repair or outlet work. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
